name: Customize manifests with Kustomize
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment. Drill EVERY Helm and Kustomize corner harder than the exam: scaffold+install a release, override values with --set and a values file, inspect release state and revisions, render without installing, apply a Kustomize base, layer transforms (namePrefix + commonLabels + replicas), generate a ConfigMap, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Kustomize: apply a base
questions.teach:
**Kustomize** customizes plain manifests with **no templating**: a `kustomization.yaml` lists `resources` and transforms. `kubectl apply -k <dir>` builds that kustomization and applies it. The base at `/tmp/kustomize-ckad` has Deployment `hello` and pins `namespace: kustomize-learn`.

**Gotcha:** `-k` takes a **directory** (or git URL), not a file — `kubectl apply -k ./dir`, never `-k file.yaml`.
questions.prompt:
Apply the Kustomize base at `/tmp/kustomize-ckad` to the cluster.

Target: Deployment `hello` exists in namespace `kustomize-learn`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy hello -n kustomize-learn

verification.description: Deployment 'hello' created in kustomize-learn from the base

questions.eli5:
Helm fills in blanks in a template. **Kustomize** is a totally different idea: there are **no blanks and no templating**. You keep your plain, ordinary YAML files exactly as they are, and then lay a recipe card on top that says "take these files, and tweak them like so."

That recipe card is a file named **`kustomization.yaml`**. In its simplest form it just lists the real manifests under `resources:` and maybe pins a namespace. The folder with the recipe card plus its manifests is called a **base**.

To use it, you point `kubectl` at the **folder** with `-k`:

`kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad`

Kubectl reads the recipe card, **builds** the combined YAML in memory, and applies it. In this base that produces a Deployment called `hello` in namespace `kustomize-learn`.

**Watch out:**

- **`-k` takes a directory (or git URL), never a single file.** `kubectl apply -k ./dir` ✅, `kubectl apply -k file.yaml` ❌. The directory must contain a `kustomization.yaml`.
- The file must be named exactly **`kustomization.yaml`** (or `kustomization.yml` / `Kustomization`) — Kustomize looks for that name.
- Kustomize does **no templating** — it never fills in `{{ }}` placeholders; it only *transforms* real YAML. Don't expect Helm-style variables.
- `kubectl apply -k` *builds then applies*. To just *see* the built output without applying, use `kubectl kustomize ./dir`.
- Everything the base sets (like `namespace: kustomize-learn`) is baked into the output — the Deployment lands in that namespace automatically.
questions.deepDive:
## Kustomize: apply a base — full rundown

### Mental model
Kustomize is **template-free** customization. You keep plain, valid Kubernetes YAML and describe transformations in a `kustomization.yaml`. Kustomize **builds** (merges base manifests + transforms) into final YAML, which you then apply. No `{{ }}`, no values — just declarative overlays on real manifests. It's built into `kubectl` (`-k` / `kubectl kustomize`).

### Anatomy of a base
```
/tmp/kustomize-ckad/
  kustomization.yaml
  deployment.yaml        # a normal Deployment named "hello"
```
```yaml
# kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: kustomize-learn      # stamps this ns onto every resource
resources:
  - deployment.yaml
```

### Build vs apply
```bash
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-ckad      # BUILD only → prints YAML to stdout
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad       # BUILD then APPLY to cluster
kustomize build /tmp/kustomize-ckad        # standalone CLI (same build)
```
Always **build first** to preview what will be applied.

### `-k` rules
| Input | Valid? |
|---|---|
| `kubectl apply -k ./dir` | ✅ directory containing `kustomization.yaml` |
| `kubectl apply -k https://github.com/org/repo//path?ref=main` | ✅ git URL |
| `kubectl apply -k file.yaml` | ❌ `-k` is not a file |
| directory with **no** `kustomization.yaml` | ❌ error |

The file must be named `kustomization.yaml`, `kustomization.yml`, or `Kustomization`.

### What a kustomization can hold (overview)
| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `resources` | base manifests / other kustomization dirs to include |
| `namespace` | set namespace on all resources |
| `namePrefix` / `nameSuffix` | rename resources |
| `commonLabels` / `labels` | stamp labels |
| `commonAnnotations` | stamp annotations |
| `images` | override image name/tag |
| `replicas` | patch replica counts |
| `patches` / `patchesStrategicMerge` | arbitrary edits |
| `configMapGenerator` / `secretGenerator` | generate CM/Secret |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`-k` takes a directory, not a file.** The single most common slip.
- The config file **must** be named `kustomization.yaml` (or accepted variants).
- **No templating** — Kustomize won't resolve Helm-style placeholders; it only transforms concrete YAML.
- `kubectl apply -k` **builds then applies**; use `kubectl kustomize dir` to inspect the build without touching the cluster.
- A `namespace:` in the kustomization **overrides** any namespace in the manifests.
- `kubectl`'s bundled Kustomize version can lag the standalone `kustomize` CLI — occasionally a newer field isn't supported by `kubectl -k`.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-ckad      # preview built YAML
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad       # build + apply
kubectl get deploy hello -n kustomize-learn
```

questions.title: Kustomize: namePrefix + commonLabels + replicas
questions.teach:
Kustomize transforms rewrite the built output without copying YAML. `namePrefix:` prepends to every resource name, `commonLabels:` stamps a label onto every resource (and selectors), and a `replicas:` entry patches a named workload's replica count.

**Gotcha:** `commonLabels` also rewrites the Deployment's **selector** — immutable once created, so a label added later to a live Deployment can force a recreate.
questions.prompt:
Edit `/tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml` to add three transforms, then re-apply with `kubectl apply -k`:
- `namePrefix: prod-` (Deployment becomes `prod-hello`)
- `commonLabels: {tier: frontend}`
- `replicas:` set workload `hello` to **5**

Target: Deployment `prod-hello` exists in `kustomize-learn` with label `tier=frontend` and `spec.replicas: 5`.
questions.hint:
Add `namePrefix: prod-`, `commonLabels:
  tier: frontend`, and `replicas:
- name: hello
  count: 5` to the kustomization, then `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad`. Verify: `kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.tier} {.spec.replicas}'`.
questions.solution:
cat >> /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml <<'YAML'
namePrefix: prod-
commonLabels:
  tier: frontend
replicas:
- name: hello
  count: 5
YAML
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.tier} {.spec.replicas}'   # frontend 5

verification.description: prod-hello in kustomize-learn has label tier=frontend and replicas 5

questions.eli5:
The recipe card can do more than list files — it can **tweak** them on the way out, without you ever editing the original YAML. Think of a photocopier with special buttons: one stamps a prefix on every name, one stamps a label on everything, one changes a count. The originals stay pristine; only the copies change.

You add three tweaks to `kustomization.yaml`:

- **`namePrefix: prod-`** — glue `prod-` to the front of every resource name. `hello` becomes `prod-hello`.
- **`commonLabels: {tier: frontend}`** — stamp the label `tier=frontend` onto every resource.
- **`replicas: - name: hello, count: 5`** — change the `hello` workload to run 5 copies.

Then re-run `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad` and the built Deployment comes out as `prod-hello`, labelled `tier=frontend`, with `replicas: 5`.

**Watch out:**

- **`commonLabels` also rewrites the Deployment's selector** (the label it uses to find its own pods). A Deployment's selector is **immutable** once it exists — so adding `commonLabels` to a *live* Deployment can force a delete-and-recreate. Set it up front where you can.
- In the `replicas:` block you name the **original** workload (`hello`), *not* the prefixed `prod-hello` — Kustomize matches before applying the prefix.
- `namePrefix` renames **everything** in the build, including generated ConfigMaps/Secrets and references to them — Kustomize rewires the references for you.
- `commonLabels` is older; newer Kustomize splits labels into `labels:` entries (with `includeSelectors`) so you can add labels *without* touching the selector. On the exam, `commonLabels` is the expected answer.
- Re-applying with a changed selector may error with "field is immutable" — if so, delete the old Deployment first.

## Kustomize transforms: namePrefix + commonLabels + replicas — full rundown

### Mental model
Transforms rewrite the **built** output without copying or editing the source manifests. You declare them in `kustomization.yaml`; `kustomize build` applies them in order and emits the final YAML. Three common transforms: rename (`namePrefix`/`nameSuffix`), stamp labels (`commonLabels`/`labels`), and patch replica counts (`replicas`).

### The kustomization additions
```yaml
# appended to /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml
namePrefix: prod-
commonLabels:
  tier: frontend
replicas:
  - name: hello        # the ORIGINAL workload name (pre-prefix)
    count: 5
```
```bash
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.tier} {.spec.replicas}'    # frontend 5
```

### What each transform does
| Transform | Effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `namePrefix: prod-` | prepends to **every** resource name | `hello` → `prod-hello`; also rewrites name references |
| `nameSuffix: -v2` | appends to every name | combinable with prefix |
| `commonLabels: {k: v}` | adds label to every resource **and its selector + pod template** | selector edit is the trap |
| `labels: [{pairs, includeSelectors}]` | newer; label without touching selector unless `includeSelectors: true` | finer control |
| `replicas: [{name, count}]` | sets `spec.replicas` on the named workload | match the **original** name |

### commonLabels and the immutable selector
`commonLabels` is applied to:
1. `metadata.labels` of every resource,
2. the Deployment/ReplicaSet/etc **`spec.selector.matchLabels`**,
3. the **pod template labels**.

Because a Deployment's `spec.selector` is **immutable after creation**, adding `commonLabels` to a workload that already exists forces a conflict:
```
field is immutable
```
Fixes: apply labels **before** first creation, or `kubectl delete deploy prod-hello` and re-apply, or use the newer `labels:` with `includeSelectors: false` to label without rewriting the selector.

### Ordering & references
- Name references (e.g. a Deployment mounting a ConfigMap) are **auto-rewired** when `namePrefix` renames the target.
- In `replicas`, `images`, and patch *targets*, you reference the **pre-prefix** name — Kustomize matches first, then renames.

### Inspect the build
```bash
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-ckad      # see prod-hello, tier label, replicas:5
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`commonLabels` rewrites the selector** → immutable-field errors on live Deployments. Know this cold.
- In `replicas:`/patches, use the **original** workload name, not the prefixed one.
- `namePrefix` renames **everything**, including generated ConfigMaps/Secrets (plus their references).
- `commonLabels` (legacy) vs `labels:` (newer, with `includeSelectors`) — `kubectl`'s bundled version may differ from standalone `kustomize`; `commonLabels` is the safe exam answer.
- Re-applying after a selector change may need a **delete + recreate**.
- YAML indentation for the appended block matters — `replicas:` is a list of `{name, count}`.

### Quick reference
```yaml
namePrefix: prod-
commonLabels:
  tier: frontend
replicas:
  - name: hello
    count: 5
```
```bash
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.tier} {.spec.replicas}'   # frontend 5
```

questions.title: Kustomize: generate a ConfigMap
questions.teach:
`configMapGenerator` builds a ConfigMap from literals or files, appending a content **hash** suffix to its name so a data change forces a rollout. `generatorOptions: {disableNameSuffixHash: true}` keeps a stable name when you need to reference it by a fixed value.

**Gotcha:** the generated name also picks up `namePrefix`, so with `namePrefix: prod-` the ConfigMap `app-cfg` becomes `prod-app-cfg` (plus the hash unless disabled).
questions.prompt:
Add a `configMapGenerator` to `/tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml` that creates ConfigMap `app-cfg` with literal `GREETING=hello`, and disable the name-hash suffix (`generatorOptions`). Re-apply with `kubectl apply -k`.

Target: a ConfigMap named `prod-app-cfg` (namePrefix applied, hash disabled) exists in `kustomize-learn` with `data.GREETING=hello`.
questions.hint:
Append `configMapGenerator:
- name: app-cfg
  literals:
  - GREETING=hello` and `generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true`. With the existing `namePrefix: prod-` the result is `prod-app-cfg`. Verify: `kubectl get cm prod-app-cfg -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.data.GREETING}'`.
questions.solution:
cat >> /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml <<'YAML'
configMapGenerator:
- name: app-cfg
  literals:
  - GREETING=hello
generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true
YAML
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get cm prod-app-cfg -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.data.GREETING}'   # hello

verification.description: ConfigMap prod-app-cfg (hash disabled) in kustomize-learn has GREETING=hello

questions.eli5:
Besides tweaking existing files, the recipe card can **make a brand-new ConfigMap for you** out of thin air. That's a **`configMapGenerator`** — you hand it some key=value facts and it bakes a ConfigMap into the build.

But it does one clever, surprising thing: it tacks a **random-looking hash** onto the ConfigMap's name, like `app-cfg-7h8k2m`. Why? So that if you later change the data, the name changes too, and anything using it notices and restarts — no stale config lingering. Handy, but annoying if you want to refer to the ConfigMap by a fixed name.

To keep the name stable, you turn the hash **off** with `generatorOptions: disableNameSuffixHash: true`.

Here you add a generator for ConfigMap `app-cfg` with `GREETING=hello`, and disable the hash. Because the kustomization already has `namePrefix: prod-`, the final name becomes **`prod-app-cfg`**.

**Watch out:**

- **The generated name picks up `namePrefix` too.** With `namePrefix: prod-`, `app-cfg` becomes `prod-app-cfg` (plus the hash, unless you disabled it). Expect the prefix.
- **Without `disableNameSuffixHash: true`, the name has a hash suffix** — `prod-app-cfg-abc123` — and a fixed-name lookup fails. Turn it off when a stable name is required.
- `generatorOptions` applies to **all** generators in the kustomization, not just one.
- Literals go under `literals:` as `KEY=value` strings; from files it's `files:` instead. Don't mix up the two.
- The hash exists for a *good* reason (auto-rollout on config change) — only disable it when you specifically need a predictable name.
questions.deepDive:
## Kustomize: configMapGenerator — full rundown

### Mental model
`configMapGenerator` (and its sibling `secretGenerator`) build a ConfigMap/Secret as part of the kustomization build, from **literals**, **files**, or **env files**. By default Kustomize appends a **content hash** to the generated name (`app-cfg-7h8k2m`) so that changing the data changes the name, which forces dependent workloads to roll. Disable that with `generatorOptions.disableNameSuffixHash: true` when you need a stable, referenceable name.

### The kustomization additions
```yaml
# appended to /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: app-cfg
    literals:
      - GREETING=hello
generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true
```
```bash
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get cm prod-app-cfg -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.data.GREETING}'   # hello
```
With the existing `namePrefix: prod-`, the final name is `prod-app-cfg` (hash disabled).

### Generator sources
| Source | Syntax |
|---|---|
| literals | `literals: ["GREETING=hello", "LANG=en"]` |
| file (whole file as one key) | `files: ["config.json"]` |
| file with custom key | `files: ["app=path/config.json"]` |
| env file (many KEY=VAL lines) | `envs: [".env"]` |

### The name-suffix hash
| | Hash on (default) | Hash off |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `app-cfg-<hash>` | `app-cfg` |
| Data change → name change | yes → triggers rollout | no (name stable) |
| Reference by fixed name | awkward | easy |
| Set via | default | `generatorOptions.disableNameSuffixHash: true` |

`generatorOptions` applies to **all** generators in the kustomization. It can also add `labels`/`annotations` to every generated object.

### Interaction with other transforms
- **`namePrefix`/`nameSuffix` apply to generated names** → `app-cfg` becomes `prod-app-cfg` (then `+hash` unless disabled).
- A workload that references the ConfigMap by its *original* name has the reference **auto-rewired** to the final (prefixed/hashed) name — Kustomize patches `envFrom`/`volumes`/`valueFrom` for you.

### Inspect the build
```bash
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-ckad | grep -A3 'kind: ConfigMap'
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Generated names inherit `namePrefix`/`nameSuffix`** — don't forget the prefix when you `get` it.
- **Default hash suffix** breaks fixed-name lookups; set `disableNameSuffixHash: true` when a stable name is required.
- `generatorOptions` is **global** to the kustomization, not per-generator.
- `literals:` uses `KEY=value` strings; `files:`/`envs:` read from disk — mixing them up is a common slip.
- Disabling the hash **loses** the automatic rollout-on-change behavior — only do it when you truly need a predictable name.
- Secrets use `secretGenerator` with the same options; values can be base64 literals or files.

### Quick reference
```yaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: app-cfg
    literals:
      - GREETING=hello
generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true
```
```bash
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get cm prod-app-cfg -n kustomize-learn -o jsonpath='{.data.GREETING}'   # hello
```

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a broken kustomization
questions.teach:
`kubectl apply -k <dir>` first **builds** the kustomization; if the build fails, nothing is applied and you get an error instead of resources. The usual causes: a `resources:` entry naming a file that doesn't exist, or a bad transform value.

**Gotcha:** read the build error first (`kubectl kustomize <dir>`) — it names the exact missing file or field before anything reaches the cluster.
questions.prompt:
The kustomization at `/tmp/kustomize-broken` **won't build** — `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken` errors and applies nothing. Diagnose the fault and fix the kustomization so the build succeeds and its Deployment is applied. Don't rewrite it from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: Deployment `api` exists in namespace `kustomize-learn` (built from the fixed `/tmp/kustomize-broken`).
questions.hint: `kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken` shows the build error — `resources:` lists `deploy.yaml` but the file on disk is `deployment.yaml` (or vice versa). Make the `resources:` entry match the real filename, then `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken`.
questions.solution:
# Build error: resources points at a file that doesn't exist.
ls /tmp/kustomize-broken
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken   # shows the offending filename
# Fix the resources entry to the real file name, then:
perl -i -pe 's/deploy\.yaml/deployment.yaml/' /tmp/kustomize-broken/kustomization.yaml
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken
kubectl get deploy api -n kustomize-learn

verification.description: Deployment 'api' applied in kustomize-learn (broken kustomization fixed)

questions.eli5:
Remember how `kubectl apply -k` first **builds** the recipe in memory, then applies it? That means if the recipe itself is broken, the build fails and **nothing** reaches the cluster — you get an error instead of resources. It's like a recipe that says "add the sauce from the jar in cupboard 3," but cupboard 3 is empty: the cook stops before plating anything.

So when `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken` errors and creates nothing, don't panic — the error message is your map. The classic cause here: the `resources:` list names a file that doesn't exist on disk. The recipe says `deploy.yaml` but the real file is `deployment.yaml` (or the other way round). One wrong filename and the whole build dies.

The fix is to *read the build error*, find the mismatch, and correct the `resources:` entry so it matches the real file. Then re-apply.

```
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken     # shows the exact bad filename
# edit kustomization.yaml so resources: matches the real file
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken
```

**Watch out:**

- **Build errors mean nothing was applied** — it's all-or-nothing. Don't go looking in the cluster for a half-made Deployment; fix the recipe instead.
- **Read `kubectl kustomize <dir>` first** — it builds without applying and prints the precise error (missing file, bad field) before anything touches the cluster.
- **Don't rewrite the whole file** — find the one wrong line. Rewriting risks dropping the `namespace:` or other correct bits.
- Filenames are **case- and spelling-exact**: `deploy.yaml` ≠ `deployment.yaml`. A `resources:` entry must match the file on disk letter-for-letter.
- Other common build breakers: a bad transform value, wrong indentation, or a `patches` target that matches nothing — the error text names which.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a broken kustomization — full rundown

### Mental model
`kubectl apply -k <dir>` is **two phases**: (1) **build** the kustomization into YAML, (2) **apply** that YAML. If the build fails, phase 2 never runs — the cluster is untouched and you get an error, not partial resources. So troubleshooting a kustomization is about reading the **build** error, not inspecting the cluster. `kubectl kustomize <dir>` runs *only* the build, so it's the fastest way to see the fault.

### Diagnosis workflow
```bash
# 1. apply fails, nothing created:
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken
#    error: ... accumulating resources: ... no such file or directory: deploy.yaml

# 2. build-only to see the exact error (no cluster writes):
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken

# 3. list what's actually on disk vs what resources: names:
ls /tmp/kustomize-broken
grep -n -A3 'resources:' /tmp/kustomize-broken/kustomization.yaml
```
Typical finding: `resources:` lists `deploy.yaml` but the file is `deployment.yaml`.

### The fix (edit, don't rewrite)
```bash
# make the resources entry match the real filename
perl -i -pe 's/deploy\.yaml/deployment.yaml/' /tmp/kustomize-broken/kustomization.yaml
# (or `kubectl edit`-style: open and change the one line)

kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken
kubectl get deploy api -n kustomize-learn
```

### Common kustomization build failures
| Symptom in error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `no such file or directory: X` | `resources:` names a missing/misspelled file | correct the filename / path |
| `accumulating resources: ... not in or below` | path escapes the kustomization root | use a path inside the dir |
| `invalid Kustomization ... unknown field` | typo'd or misindented field | fix field name/indent |
| `no matches for Id ...` (patch/replicas) | transform target name doesn't match a resource | match the correct (pre-prefix) name |
| `couldn't make target for path` | `resources:` points at a dir without a kustomization | add one or point at a file |
| duplicate resource | same object listed twice | dedupe `resources:` |

### Why build-before-apply matters
Because the build is atomic, a kustomization is **all-or-nothing**: you never get a half-applied set from a build error. That's a feature — fix the recipe and re-apply cleanly.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Nothing is applied on a build error** — don't hunt the cluster for partial objects; fix the kustomization.
- **`kubectl kustomize <dir>` first** — it surfaces the precise error offline before touching the cluster.
- **Filenames are exact** (`deploy.yaml` ≠ `deployment.yaml`); `resources:` must match disk letter-for-letter.
- **Fix the one wrong line**, don't rewrite — rewriting risks dropping correct fields (like `namespace:`).
- `resources:` can list **files or directories** (a dir must itself contain a `kustomization.yaml`).
- Transform targets (`replicas`, `patches`) reference resources by **pre-prefix** name; a mismatch is a build error too.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl kustomize /tmp/kustomize-broken     # read the build error (no apply)
ls /tmp/kustomize-broken                      # compare real filenames
# fix resources: to match the actual file, then:
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-broken
kubectl get deploy api -n kustomize-learn
```
